intervals.label: CANGAROO telescopes in operation
intervals.note: Start from the CANGAROO-I 3.8 m telescope (1992); end from the statement that activities in Australia stopped in 2011.
intervals.quote: It started from a 3.8-m telescope[1] (CANGAROO-I) in 1992.

intervals.label: observing activities ended
intervals.note: No source states that the site was dismantled; only that CANGAROO activities in Australia stopped in 2011.
intervals.quote: Eventually, the activities in Australia were stopped in 2011.

name: Woomera CANGAROO Site
notes: No operator is recorded: the sources describe a Japanese-Australian collaboration (University of Adelaide and Japanese universities, arXiv:2406.15037) but name no legal operator of the site.
No live website: the collaboration home page survives only on the Internet Archive (the icrhp9.icrr.u-tokyo.ac.jp host no longer resolves).

summary.plain: The dark outback site near Woomera, South Australia, where the Japanese-Australian CANGAROO collaboration ran its gamma-ray telescopes from 1992 until 2011.
summary.technical: Observing site of the CANGAROO imaging atmospheric Cherenkov telescopes near Woomera, South Australia, 160 m a.s.l.: the 3.8 m telescope (CANGAROO-I), the 7 m / 10 m CANGAROO-II telescope and the four-telescope 10 m CANGAROO-III array. Observations stopped in 2011.
